ABSTRACT
This study explores the transformative role of AI-­enhanced social–emotional learning (SEL) frameworks in improving the en-
gagement and emotional well-­being of English as a foreign language (EFL) students in China. A survey was conducted among 
816 undergraduate and postgraduate students from universities across five provinces, utilising convenience sampling. The re-
search focused on how AI tools integrated into English learning contribute to student engagement and emotional stability. Data 
were analysed using SPSS for descriptive and regression analyses and AMOS for structural equation modelling. The findings 
highlight that AI-­enhanced SEL significantly boosts student engagement and emotional well-­being. By providing tailored learn-
ing experiences based on students' emotional and cognitive needs, AI systems facilitate better emotional regulation, increased 
focus and improved academic performance. The results suggest that AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks offer personalised support 
that not only enhances learning outcomes but also creates a more emotionally supportive environment, contributing to students' 
overall academic success and well-­being.
1   |   Introduction
In an increasingly interconnected and technologically ad-
vanced world, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into 
educational frameworks is revolutionising traditional teaching 
methodologies (Fathi, Rahimi, and Derakhshan 2024; Liu and 
Wang 2024; Xin and Derakhshan 2024; Wang 2023). Among the 
most significant innovations is the enhancement of social–emo-
tional learning (SEL), particularly within the context of English 
as a foreign language (EFL) education. This transformation 
is not merely about linguistic proficiency; it encompasses the 
holistic development of students, emphasising their emotional 
intelligence, resilience and ability to engage with diverse peers 
and cultures (Guo and Jiang 2023; Pourtousi, Babanezhad, and 
Ghanizadeh 2024). As EFL students navigate the complexities 
of learning a new language, they face unique emotional and 
social challenges that can impact their motivation and overall 
well-­being (Liu and Wang 2024). An AI-­enhanced SEL frame-
work addresses these challenges by personalising learning expe-
riences, providing real-­time feedback, and fostering a supportive 
learning environment (Cheng and Liu 2024). By leveraging data 
analytics, natural language processing, and adaptive learning 
technologies, educators can create tailored interventions that 
enhance student engagement and promote emotional resilience 
(Derakhshan and Fathi 2024a, 2024b; Huang 2023).
In the contemporary educational landscape, the challenges 
faced by EFL students are multifaceted, encompassing linguistic

barriers, cultural differences and social–emotional hurdles (Al-­
Bogami and Elyas 2020; Wang and Derakhshan 2024; Zhang, 
Hu, and Yu 2024). Many EFL learners struggle with motivation, 
engagement and emotional resilience, which can hinder their 
ability to acquire language skills effectively (Derakhshan and 
Ghiasvand  2024; Dewaele and Li  2021). Traditional teaching 
methods often neglect the emotional and social dimensions of 
learning, leading to disengagement and adverse psychological 
impacts on students' overall well-­being. SEL has emerged as a 
vital component in creating supportive learning environments 
that foster both emotional intelligence and academic success 
(Dao and Sato 2021). However, there is a significant gap in the 
integration of AI technologies within SEL frameworks specifi-
cally tailored for EFL contexts. Although AI has the potential 
to provide personalised and adaptive learning experiences, its 
application in addressing the emotional needs of EFL students 
has been underexplored (Bai, Shen, and Wang 2024; Fernández-­
García and Fonseca-­Mora 2022). Therefore, the central problem 
this study seeks to address is the lack of empirical understand-
ing of how an AI-­enhanced SEL framework can impact EFL stu-
dents' engagement and emotional well-­being.
The increasing emphasis on both SEL and the integration 
of technology in education highlights a critical need to ex-
plore innovative approaches that foster holistic development 
in learners (Balasubramanian and Al-­Mahrooqi  2016; Qi and 
Derakhshan 2024). The challenge of teaching EFL extends be-
yond mere linguistic skills; it encompasses the emotional and 
social dimensions that significantly influence student engage-
ment and learning outcomes (Yabukoshi and Mizumoto 2023). 
Recognising and addressing these dimensions is essential for 
creating a conducive learning environment that promotes not 
only language proficiency but also emotional well-­being and 
interpersonal skills. Integrating AI into the SEL framework of-
fers a promising pathway to enhance the learning experience 
for EFL students. AI technologies can facilitate personalised 
learning strategies that adapt to individual student needs, al-
lowing for tailored interventions that address emotional chal-
lenges and learning barriers (Derakhshan and Noughabi 2024; 
Xu and Li 2024). By harnessing the power of AI, educators are 
better equipped to monitor student engagement and emotional 
states in real time, leading to timely support and encourage-
ment that can significantly reduce anxiety and increase moti-
vation among EFL learners. This study aims to investigate the 
relationship between an AI-­enhanced SEL framework and its 
impact on EFL students' engagement and emotional well-­being. 
By exploring how AI tools can facilitate SEL practices, the re-
search seeks to provide empirical evidence on the effectiveness 
of such an approach in fostering a positive learning environ-
ment. Understanding this relationship may illuminate the crit-
ical role of emotional intelligence in language acquisition and 
the potential for AI to revolutionise pedagogical strategies in the 
EFL context.
2   |   Review of the Literature
The theoretical framework for this study provides a compre-
hensive understanding of the variables of the study. SEL en-
compasses the processes through which individuals develop the 
skills to recognise and manage their emotions, establish positive 
relationships and make responsible decisions (Derakhshan, 
Setiawan, and Ghafouri 2024; Liu and Wang 2024). According 
to the collaborative for academic, social, and emotional learning 
(CASEL), the core competencies of SEL include self-­awareness, 
self-­management, social awareness, relationship skills and re-
sponsible decision-­making. Research has demonstrated that 
SEL contributes significantly to enhanced academic perfor-
mance, improved mental health and strengthened interpersonal 
relationships (Lu, Wang, and Wang 2024). In the context of EFL 
education, implementing SEL practices can help students nav-
igate the emotional challenges associated with learning a new 
language, thereby improving their engagement and outcomes 
(Zhou and Hou  2024). Second Language Acquisition theory 
highlights that language learning is not solely a cognitive pro-
cess but also an emotional one (Shao et al. 2023). The Affective 
Filter Hypothesis, proposed by Stephen Krashen, posits that 
emotional states can significantly influence language learning. 
A positive emotional environment can lower the affective fil-
ter, facilitating greater language acquisition (Derakhshan, Teo, 
and Khazaie  2024; Mohammadi Zenouzagh, Admiraal, and 
Saab 2024; Zheng and Guo 2024). Conversely, anxiety and neg-
ative emotions can hinder learning. Therefore, fostering emo-
tional well-­being through SEL can be particularly crucial for 
EFL students who may experience heightened levels of anxiety 
in foreign language classroom settings. The integration of AI in 
educational contexts has gained traction, offering innovative 
solutions to enhance personalised learning experiences. AI tech-
nologies can analyse student behaviour, provide real-­time feed-
back and adapt teaching strategies based on individual needs. In 
the realm of SEL, AI can play a pivotal role in monitoring and 
responding to students' emotional states, offering tailored inter-
ventions that align with their social–emotional needs. By util-
ising data analytics and machine learning, AI-­enhanced SEL 
frameworks can create more engaging and responsive learning 
environments (Yüce, Nazari, and Karimpour 2024).
This study positions AI-­enhanced SEL as an innovative ap-
proach to improving EFL students' engagement and emotional 
well-­being (Derakhshan et  al.  2024; Zhao and Wang  2024). 
The conceptual framework suggests that AI-­enhanced SEL 
Practices involve the use of AI tools to deliver personalised SEL 
interventions, providing real-­time insights into students' emo-
tional health and engagement levels. EFL Student Engagement 
increased engagement is predicted as students receive more 
tailored, responsive support that addresses their emotional and 
social needs within the EFL context. Enhanced emotional well-­
being is anticipated as students experience reduced anxiety, 
increased motivation, and a greater sense of belonging in the 
classroom (Derakhshan and Yin 2024; Hu et al. 2024; Liu, Li, 
and Fang 2024). By integrating these theoretical perspectives, 
this study aims to contribute to the understanding of how AI-­
enhanced SEL frameworks can serve as a powerful catalyst for 
improving engagement and emotional health among EFL learn-
ers, thereby transforming the educational experience and out-
comes in the language learning process (Zhi and Wang 2024).
Recent empirical studies explore various dimensions of AI 
integration, SEL, EFL education and emotional health, con-
tributing to a broader understanding of this evolving field. 
Wu (2024) examined the use of AI-­driven SEL programs in 
EFL classrooms, demonstrating improvements in students'

plored the interplay of gamification and AI in EFL contexts, 
showing positive correlations between enhanced engage-

Liu et  al.  (2024) evaluated how personalised AI interven-
tions in SEL frameworks significantly enhance EFL students' 
engagement, self-­awareness and emotional resilience. Zhi 
and Wang  (2024) investigated how AI-­enhanced SEL strat-
egies positively affect language acquisition and emotional 
well-­being, indicating higher levels of student participation 
and lower anxiety levels. Wang and Hui  (2024) highlighted 
the critical role of AI tools in fostering a safe and engaging 
learning atmosphere for EFL students, resulting in improved 
emotional well-­being and engagement metrics. Xu, Li, and 
Yang (2024) determined the impact of AI-­based SEL programs 
on enhancing emotional intelligence and engagement among 
EFL learners, illustrating positive correlations with emotional 
well-­being. Liu and Chang  (2024) focused on how learning 
analytics powered by AI can predict and enhance social–emo-
tional skills in EFL students, impacting their engagement and 
overall educational experience. Liu et al. (2024) explored the 
relationship between AI-­enhanced SEL initiatives and EFL 
students' engagement levels, finding a significant impact on 
emotional health and academic performance. Dolenc and 
Brumen  (2024) investigated the effectiveness of AI-­enabled 
SEL frameworks in providing emotional support to EFL stu-
dents, resulting in increased engagement and improved emo-
tional health outcomes.
Reviewing the literature brings forth several controversial 
issues within the literature and empirical studies. Empirical 
studies report varied results regarding the effectiveness of 
AI-­enhanced SEL programs. Some studies show significant 
improvements in student engagement and emotional well-­
being, whereas others indicate little to no change (Wang and 
Wang 2024; Yuan and Liu 2025). This discrepancy leads to de-
bates about the generalizability and effectiveness of these in-
terventions in diverse classrooms (Wu, Wang, and Wang 2024; 
Yang and Zhao 2024). Scholars contest the quality and com-
prehensiveness of AI-­driven SEL frameworks compared to 
human-­led interventions. Critics argue that AI may lack the 
nuance and empathy required to effectively support students' 
emotional needs, potentially leading to superficial engage-
ment without addressing deeper issues (Wang et  al.  2023). 
The reliance on AI technologies in SEL frameworks raises 
questions about the role of teachers in mediating emotional 
learning. Some educators are concerned that emphasising AI's 
role might diminish their professional judgement and pres-
ence in the classroom, which are critical for fostering genuine 
emotional connections with students (Guo et  al.  2024). The 
integration of AI in SEL also calls for adequate training for ed-
ucators to effectively implement these tools. There are debates 
regarding whether current teacher preparation programs suf-
ficiently equip educators to navigate AI-­enhanced learning 
environments (Dahri et al. 2024; Wang and Xue 2024). Many 
argued that emotional well-­being is best cultivated through 
human interactions, which AI systems may not fully replicate 
(Dahri et al. 2024; Fan and Zhang 2024). This raised concerns 
about students becoming overly reliant on technology for emo-
tional support rather than developing face-­to-­face social skills 
and resilience. Some AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks utilise 
screening tools to detect students' emotions. Critics caution 
that such tools might inaccurately assess emotions, leading to 
inappropriate or unnecessary interventions, which could ex-
acerbate feelings of isolation or inadequacy among students 
(Darwin et al. 2024; Shen et al. 2024).
3   |   Research Questions
RQ1. Is there any significant relationship between AI-­enhanced 
SEL framework, EFL students' engagement and their emotional 
well-­being?
RQ2. To what extent does EFL students' AI-­enhanced SEL 
framework predict their engagement and emotional well-­being?
By addressing these questions, this research aims to provide in-
sights into the efficacy of integrating AI with SEL approaches 
in the EFL context, ultimately contributing to enhanced edu-
cational strategies that prioritise student engagement and emo-
tional health.
4   |   Method
4.1   |   Participants
This study utilised survey data from a comprehensive project 
examining AI-­enhanced English learning among undergrad-
uate and postgraduate students across various universities 
from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Heilongjiang 
Province, Shanxi Province, Jiangsu Province and Guangdong 
Province in China. Utilising convenience sampling methods, 
the online survey was disseminated via colleagues who teach 
public English courses at the targeted university. A total of 816 
participants (449 males, 55.02%; 367 females, 44.98%) com-
pleted the online survey. The participants' ages varied, with 
the majority falling within the 17–21 years range (67.89%), 
followed by those aged 22–26 years (30.76%) and 27–31 years 
(1.35%). Regarding academic qualifications, 67.89% held a 
Bachelor's degree, whereas 32.11% held a Master's degree. 
Participants were enrolled in various programs, including en-
gineering (31.04%), journalism (29.39%), agriculture (22.93%), 
medicine (15.23%), and others (1.41%). All participants indi-
cated that English was their foreign language and that they 
had been engaged in English language study for a minimum 
of 10 years.
4.2   |   Instruments
4.2.1   |   AI-­Enhanced Social–Emotional Learning (SEL) 
Questionnaire
The SEL questionnaire consists of 25 Likert-­scale items distrib-
uted across five subscales: AI literacy & SEL understanding, 
emotional awareness & management, social skills & relation-
ships, engagement & motivation and emotional well-­being 
(Licardo and Lipovec 2023). The questionnaire measures vari-
ous aspects of social–emotional learning (SEL) in AI-­enhanced

with established SEL frameworks and expert reviews. Construct 
validity was supported through factor analysis, revealing the 
expected five-­factor structure. The questionnaire also demon-

4.2.2   |   AI-­Enhanced Student Engagement 
Questionnaire
The AI-­enhanced student engagement questionnaire is a tool 
comprising 25 Likert-­scale items, each designed to measure var-
ious aspects of student engagement in AI-­enhanced learning 
environments (Mirdad et  al.  2024). The questionnaire consists 
of four subscales: cognitive, behavioural, emotional and social 
engagement. Its validity was confirmed through content valida-
tion by experts and construct validation via factor analysis, which 
demonstrated that each subscale accurately measures its intended 
aspect of engagement. The questionnaire also shows strong inter-
nal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha values above 0.70, indicat-
ing reliable measurement within each subscale (r = 0.88).
4.3   |   Emotional Well-­Being Questionnaire
The Emotional well-­being questionnaire consists of 25 Likert-­
scale items designed to assess various dimensions of emotional 
well-­being across five key subscales: emotional awareness & 
understanding, emotional regulation, positive emotions, neg-
ative emotions and social connectedness (Doll, Petersen, and 
Stewart-­Brown 2000). The Emotional Well-­Being Questionnaire 
evaluates various aspects of emotional well-­being and social–
emotional skills. Content validity was ensured through expert 
review, aligning items with established frameworks. Factor 
analysis confirmed construct validity, showing the items fit into 
the intended subscales. The questionnaire demonstrated strong 
internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha values above 0.70 
for all subscales (r = 0.91), making it a reliable and valid tool for 
assessing emotional health across different areas.
4.4   |   Procedure
4.4.1   |   Study Context and Scope
The study was conducted as part of a comprehensive project in-
vestigating the integration of AI tools in English learning among 
undergraduate and postgraduate students across universities in 
China. The study regions included Inner Mongolia Autonomous 
Region, Heilongjiang Province, Shanxi Province, Jiangsu 
Province and Guangdong Province, ensuring a geographically 
diverse sample.
4.4.2   |   Research Focus
The research explored the impact of AI tools on student engage-
ment and learning outcomes in English language education.
4.4.3   |   Sampling and Survey Distribution
Sampling Method: Convenience sampling was used to recruit 
participants, facilitated by university colleagues teaching pub-
lic English courses in the specified provinces (Creswell and 
Creswell 2017; Etikan, Musa, and Alkassim 2016).
Survey Distribution: Surveys were distributed online, offering 
an efficient way to reach a large number of participants.
4.4.4   |   Participant Characteristics
A total of 816 students participated, representing diverse educa-
tional backgrounds.
All participants confirmed that English was their foreign lan-
guage and that they had been studying it for at least 10 years, 
ensuring sufficient exposure to language learning.
4.4.5   |   Ethical Considerations
Participants were informed of the study's objectives and as-
sured that their personal information would remain confi-
dential. Informed consent was obtained to ensure voluntary 
participation.
4.4.6   |   Data Collection
Once all questionnaires were completed, the data was securely 
stored for analysis.
4.4.7   |   Data Analysis
Tools Used: SPSS (version 27) and AMOS (version 24).
4.4.8   |   Statistical Procedures
SPSS was utilised for descriptive statistics, correlations and re-
gression analyses to identify relationships and trends. AMOS 
was employed for structural equation modelling (SEM) to 
analyse complex relationships among variables. Advanced 
Techniques: Factor analysis was conducted to reduce data di-
mensions and identify underlying constructs.
4.4.9   |   Findings Interpretation
The analysed data was examined to uncover significant pat-
terns, correlations, and relationships among variables, yielding 
valuable insights into the study's hypotheses.
5   |   Results
The researcher used confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to test if 
the observed variables aligned with their theoretical constructs.

The standardised regression weights reveal robust positive as-

the constructs—AI-­enhanced SEL, emotional well-­being, and 
AI-­enhanced student engagement—are closely interconnected. 
As a result, improvements in one of these areas could likely 
trigger positive changes in the others, highlighting the dynamic 
nature of their interaction. The strength of these relationships, 
along with their statistical significance, underscores the crit-
ical role these variables play in shaping a comprehensive un-
derstanding of how AI-­driven interventions can enhance SEL, 
foster emotional well-­being, and improve student engagement. 
These findings suggest that focusing on one domain could have 
cascading benefits across the educational environment, making 
the integration of AI technologies a powerful tool for promoting 
holistic student development.
Figure 2 demonstrates strong relationships across variables, as 
indicated by the high factor loadings of the observed indicators 
on their respective latent constructs. These high factor loadings 
show that the observed variables are good measures of the un-
derlying theoretical constructs. For instance, values exceeding 
0.7 are typically considered strong, which supports the conver-
gent validity of the model—ensuring that the items strongly re-
late to the construct they are supposed to measure. Additionally, 
the high factor loadings contribute to the reliability of the model, 
meaning the items consistently represent their constructs across 
different samples or measures. Reliability can be further con-
firmed through tests like Cronbach's alpha, where a threshold of 
0.7 or higher typically reflects satisfactory reliability. The mod-
el's ability to separate the constructs and demonstrate low cor-
relations between them, along with the squared correlations and 
AVE values, also indicates discriminant validity. This confirms 
that the constructs are distinct from one another, reinforcing the 
overall robustness of the measurement model. Figure 2 effec-
tively validates both the theoretical and empirical relationships 
between the variables, ensuring that the constructs are mea-
sured accurately and consistently.
The estimate for emotional well-­being in Table 4 is 0.613, sug-
gesting a moderately strong positive effect of this variable on the 
outcome being measured. The estimate for AI-­enhanced student 
engagement is 0.662, representing a strong positive effect on the 
measured outcome. Both variables show statistically significant 
positive effects, with reliable estimates based on their respective 
confidence intervals. The findings from Table  4 indicate that 
a notable percentage, approximately 61%, of the variations ob-
served in teachers' emotional well-­being can be directly linked to 
the impact of AI-­enhanced SEL programs. This suggests that the 
integration of AI into SEL frameworks plays a crucial role in fos-
tering teachers' emotional health. Such programs may provide 
teachers with tailored strategies and resources that help them 
manage stress, improve interpersonal relationships, and en-
hance their overall job satisfaction. Furthermore, the data reveal 
that about 66% of the variations observed in teachers' student en-
gagement levels can similarly be attributed to the effects of AI-­
enhanced SEL. This implies that the tools and methodologies

connections between teachers and students, ultimately leading 
to improved educational outcomes. The interplay between emo-
tional well-­being and student engagement underscores the im-
portance of investing in SEL that leverages technology to benefit 
both educators and learners.
6   |   Discussion
The findings demonstrate that AI-­enhanced SEL improves en-
gagement by providing personalised support tailored to students' 
emotional and academic needs. This can be rationalised through 
social constructivist theory, which emphasises the role of social 
and emotional contexts in learning. By creating emotionally 
supportive and interactive environments, AI tools facilitate ac-
tive participation and engagement. The study highlights the role 
of SEL in reducing anxiety and fostering a sense of belonging, 
both of which are crucial for language acquisition according to 
the affective filter hypothesis. The rationale here lies in how AI 
technologies detect and respond to students' emotional states, 
lowering barriers to learning and enhancing their academic 
performance. The discussion explains how AI's data-­driven ca-
pabilities enhance SEL by offering real-­time, adaptive feedback. 
This aligns with research suggesting that such technologies 
bridge gaps in traditional SEL practices by addressing individual 
emotional and cognitive differences more effectively.
AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks offer a transformative approach 
to improving the engagement and emotional well-­being of EFL 
students. By analysing emotional states and cognitive needs, AI 
personalises learning experiences, addressing students' unique 
challenges such as anxiety and motivation. This real-­time adapt-
ability promotes sustained engagement and motivation, helping 
students overcome language barriers. Additionally, AI tools 
aid in emotional regulation, providing insights into negative 
emotions and fostering emotional awareness, which empowers 
students to manage their feelings effectively, improving both ac-
ademic success and emotional health.
The consistent, individualised support offered by AI systems is 
particularly important in helping students develop emotional 
resilience—a crucial factor in navigating the complexities 
of learning a new language. When students feel emotionally 
secure and supported, their well-­being improves, allowing 
them to focus more fully on their language learning. As emo-
tional well-­being increases, students are more likely to engage 
positively in classroom activities, participate in discussions, 
and take risks in their learning, all of which contribute to 
enhanced language acquisition. The intertwining of engage-
ment and emotional well-­being has profound implications for 
academic outcomes. Research indicates that emotional sta-
bility is linked to improved cognitive performance; students 
who manage their emotions effectively tend to exhibit better 
concentration and retention of information. Therefore, AI-­
enhanced SEL frameworks do not just elevate emotional and

efits. Furthermore, these frameworks create a more conducive 
learning environment where emotional and academic support 
coexist. As EFL students navigate their learning journey in a 
supportive atmosphere, they are less likely to experience aca-
demic burnout or drop-­out rates, leading to overall improved 
academic performance.
The predictive relationship between the AI-­enhanced SEL 
framework and EFL students' engagement and emotional 
well-­being is a vital finding of this integration. With AI's 
ability to analyse vast amounts of data related to student be-
haviour and emotional responses, educators can anticipate 
both positive and negative trends in student engagement. This 
foresight allows for timely interventions, enabling teachers to 
provide support before issues escalate, ensuring that EFL stu-
dents remain engaged and emotionally stable throughout their 
learning process. This predictive ability further emphasises 
the role of educators as facilitators of AI integration, where 
they function as guides in leveraging the insights provided 
by AI tools to foster an emotionally intelligent classroom en-
vironment. For instance, educators can utilise AI-­generated 
reports to identify students who may be struggling and adjust 
their instructional strategies accordingly, ensuring that sup-
port aligns with student needs.
Despite the promising findings, several challenges must be ad-
dressed to fully realise the potential of AI-­enhanced SEL frame-
works. These include ethical considerations related to data 
privacy, the potential for bias in AI algorithms, and questions 
about the replacement of human empathy in the learning pro-
cess. Educators must carefully navigate these challenges to en-
sure that the integration of AI tools complements rather than 
replaces the crucial human elements of teaching. Additionally, 
it is essential to consider the cultural context of EFL students 
when designing AI-­enhanced SEL interventions. Culturally tai-
lored content and support are critical to avoiding oversimplifica-
tion of emotional experiences and ensuring that students from 
diverse backgrounds feel understood and valued in the learning 
environment.
The findings surrounding the positive impacts of AI-­enhanced 
SEL frameworks on EFL students' engagement and emotional 
well-­being align largely with previous research, while also pro-
viding new insights that build upon the existing literature. The 
recent exploration into AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks illustrates 
a significant positive effect on both engagement and emotional 
well-­being among EFL students. Studies indicate that these 
frameworks improve students' focus and emotional resilience, 
contributing to better academic outcomes and emotional sta-
bility. Similar conclusions have emerged in earlier studies ex-
amining the role of SEL in education. For instance, research by 
Wang (2023) highlighted that effective SEL programs can sig-
nificantly boost students' emotional well-­being and academic 
performance. Moreover, a meta-­analysis by Liu et  al.  (2024) 
specifically reinforced that SEL interventions increase student 
engagement and support positive emotional adjustment, un-
derscoring the critical role of SEL in enhancing student out-
comes. The current findings solidify these earlier conclusions 
while emphasising the specific advantages of integrating AI 
technologies into SEL frameworks. Although previous studies 
have established the effectiveness of SEL, the role of AI as a fa-
cilitator of personalised learning experiences brings an innova-
tive perspective that enhances these well-­documented benefits 
(Huang  2023). This represents a significant advancement in 
understanding how SEL can be effectively implemented in EFL 
contexts.
The integration of AI tools facilitates emotional regulation 
and provides personalised feedback, which in turn boosts en-
gagement and emotional well-­being among EFL learners. The 
ability of AI to tailor learning experiences based on students' 
emotional states is particularly noteworthy. Earlier research has 
consistently indicated the importance of emotional regulation 
in educational success. For example, Dolenc and Brumen (2024) 
pointed out that self-­regulation strategies significantly influence 
students' learning outcomes. Additionally, studies focused on 
technology-­enhanced learning environments, such as those by 
Bai, Shen, and Wang (2024), suggest that personalised feedback 
provided by intelligent tutoring systems leads to increased stu-
dent engagement and motivation. The current findings expand 
on these studies by explicitly linking emotional regulation and 
personalised feedback to AI's capabilities within SEL frame-
works. Although previous literature acknowledged the impor-
tance of personalised support, the unique contribution of AI 
systems that adapt to individual emotional states represents a 
nuanced advancement. This raises the discussion on how tech-
nology can enhance traditional pedagogical approaches (Zhi 
and Wang 2024).
The study suggests that EFL students' engagement and 
emotional well-­being can be significantly predicted by AI-­
enhanced SEL frameworks, emphasising AI's ability to tailor 
experiences based on emotional and cognitive needs. Previous 
research, like that of Yabukoshi and Mizumoto  (2023), in-
dicated that teachers' ability to assess and adapt their in-
structional strategies leads to better student outcomes, but 
it often lacked the dynamic adaptability offered by AI solu-
tions. Moreover, some studies have pointed towards the role 
of data analytics in education for improving student perfor-
mance, but without the integrated emotional focus observed 
in AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks (Balasubramanian and Al-­
Mahrooqi  2016; Hu et  al.  2024; Yang and Zhao  2024). The 
current findings provide a fresh perspective by showing not 
only the predictive capability of AI in student engagement 
and emotional well-­being but also highlighting the real-­time 
adaptability of AI compared to traditional assessment strate-
gies used in previous studies. This presents a significant shift 
in how educators can leverage data for personalised learning, 
further enriching the conversation established by earlier re-
search (Guo et al. 2024).
The findings suggest that AI systems provide consistent, indi-
vidualised support, helping EFL students manage stress and 
emotions within the context of learning. This leads to a more 
conducive environment for language acquisition. Research has 
shown that a supportive learning environment is crucial for stu-
dents, especially those facing language barriers (Dewaele and 
Li 2021). Studies have demonstrated that emotional support in 
educational settings can reduce anxiety and create more favour-
able conditions for learning (Dahri et al. 2024). Although these 
previous studies recognised the importance of a supportive

Finally, the current findings on the integration of AI-­enhanced 
SEL frameworks into the educational experiences of EFL stu-
dents align with prior studies that emphasise the importance 
of SEL in improving engagement and emotional well-­being. 
However, they significantly advance the discourse by illustrat-
ing the specific and dynamic roles AI can play in personalising 
learning, facilitating emotional regulation, and predicting stu-
dent needs. As education continues to evolve technologically, 
these findings emphasise the growing necessity and potential 
for AI-­integrated approaches, while also underscoring the need 
to address ethical considerations and ensure that technology 
complements, rather than detracts from, human connections in 
the educational process. The ongoing dialogue between tradi-
tional SEL methods and modern AI applications will be vital in 
shaping effective educational practices for future generations.
7   |   Implications
The findings surrounding the integration of AI-­enhanced SEL 
frameworks provide significant theoretical implications for sev-
eral fields, including educational psychology, applied linguistics 
and technology-­enhanced learning. These implications high-
light the necessity of re-­evaluating existing theories and prac-
tices to accommodate the innovative methodologies presented 
by AI technologies in education. The study supports and extends 
traditional SEL theories, such as the CASEL model, which em-
phasises the importance of emotional intelligence in educational 
success. By demonstrating how AI can facilitate the primary 
competencies of SEL, such as self-­awareness and emotional 
regulation, the integration of AI challenges educators to adopt 
a more nuanced understanding of how emotional intelligence 
can be cultivated in classroom settings. Moreover, it suggests the 
need to update SEL frameworks to incorporate technology as an 
integral component of emotional development, thus merging 
contemporary pedagogical practices with theoretical models.
From the perspective of Second Language Acquisition (SLA), 
these findings underscore the importance of addressing emo-
tional and psychological factors in language learning processes. 
The affective filter hypothesis by Krashen highlights how emo-
tions can influence language learning; however, the findings 
suggest that AI technologies can actively lower this affective 
filter. By providing real-­time emotional regulation support, AI 
tools may serve as positive interventions, enhancing student 
engagement and reducing anxiety related to language learn-
ing. This integration prompts a re-­evaluation of SLA theories 
to include technology as a pivotal tool for emotional support, 
thereby presenting a comprehensive approach that intertwines 
emotional well-­being with language acquisition. The identified 
ability of AI systems to deliver personalised feedback reinforces 
the significance of differentiated instruction theories in educa-
tional psychology. Learning theories, such as constructivism, 
advocate for tailored educational experiences that account for 
individual learner differences. The current findings suggest that 
AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks provide a practical application 
of these theories, illustrating how technology can support per-
sonalised learning at scale. This intersection underlines the po-
tential for AI to transform theoretical models of personalization 
into actionable strategies that promote student engagement and 
success.
The study contributes to the theoretical discourse surrounding 
student engagement by presenting a robust connection between 
emotional well-­being and engagement levels. Previous engage-
ment theories often focused on cognitive and behavioural as-
pects, neglecting the emotional dimensions crucial for sustained 
engagement. The findings indicate that emotional support pro-
vided through AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks significantly pre-
dicts and boosts engagement, suggesting that future theoretical 
models should encompass emotional factors more comprehen-
sively. This adjustment invites researchers to create integrated 
models that emphasise the emotional, cognitive and behavioural 
components of student engagement. The findings challenge ex-
isting educational theories regarding the role of technology in 
the classroom. Traditionally, technology has been viewed pri-
marily as a tool for enhancing content delivery. However, the 
current research presents evidence that AI technologies, when 
embedded within SEL frameworks, can play a critical role in fos-
tering emotional growth and student well-­being. This shift en-
courages a re-­examination of educational technology theories, 
advocating for a more holistic understanding of how technology 
can support not only academic but also emotional and social 
learning experiences. The integration of emotional regulation 
and resilience into educational practices inspired by AI tech-
nologies has broader implications for lifelong learning theories. 
Understanding how individuals manage emotions and develop 
resilience is essential for continuous personal and professional 
growth. The current findings suggest that embedding SEL into 
educational frameworks prepares students for the emotional 
challenges of learning throughout their lives. This connection 
serves as a foundation for future exploration into how emotional 
competencies, nurtured through AI-­enhanced SEL, contribute 
to lifelong learning and adaptability.
The integration of AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks in EFL ed-
ucation offers several impactful benefits. AI tools can tailor 
learning environments to meet individual students' emotional 
and cognitive needs, resulting in higher sustained engagement 
in the classroom. By addressing students' emotional states, AI 
helps keep students focused and engaged in the learning pro-
cess. The personalised emotional support provided by AI fosters 
better emotional regulation, which positively impacts student 
well-­being. This leads to a more emotionally stable environment 
conducive to learning, reducing stress and anxiety. By improv-
ing both engagement and emotional resilience, AI-­enhanced 
SEL frameworks contribute to better academic performance. 
Emotionally well-­supported students tend to be more motivated 
and perform better academically.

9   |   Conclusion
The integration of AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks represents a 
groundbreaking shift in the educational landscape, particularly 
for EFL students. As demonstrated in the findings of this study, 
the application of AI technologies within SEL principles has a 
profound and multifaceted impact on enhancing students' en-
gagement and emotional well-­being. The evidence indicates that 
AI tools not only facilitate emotional regulation but also deliver 
personalised feedback tailored to meet the individual needs 
of EFL learners. This personalization is critical in fostering a 
learning environment where students feel understood and sup-
ported, ultimately leading to improved focus and sustained en-
gagement. The predictive capabilities of AI allow educators to 
tailor their approaches, ensuring that support mechanisms are 
timely and effective, thereby addressing the unique challenges 
EFL students face in their learning journeys.
Furthermore, the findings highlight a direct correlation between 
effective emotional support and the overall academic perfor-
mance of students. By equipping learners with emotional resil-
ience and coping strategies, AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks create 
a more conducive learning environment, reducing stress and 
promoting stability. These frameworks empower students to take 
an active role in their emotional development, leading to better 
academic outcomes and a more positive classroom atmosphere. 
In conclusion, the transformative potential of AI-­enhanced SEL 
frameworks in shaping EFL students' experiences cannot be over-
stated. As educational institutions continue to navigate the intri-
cacies of digital learning environments, it is essential to prioritise 
the integration of emotionally intelligent technologies that facili-
tate not just academic success, but holistic student development. 
The future of education lies in creating adaptive, emotionally 
supportive learning experiences that recognise and celebrate the 
unique emotional landscapes of each student, ultimately fostering 
a generation of resilient, engaged and capable learners.

Abstract: This study explores the transformative role of AI-­enhanced social–emotional learning (SEL) frameworks in improving the en- gagement and emotional well-­being of English as a foreign language (EFL) students in China. A survey was conducted among 816 undergraduate and postgraduate students from universities across five provinces, utilising convenience sampling. The re- search focused on how AI tools integrated into English learning contribute to student engagement and emotional stability. Data were analysed using SPSS for descriptive and regression analyses and AMOS for structural equation modelling. The findings highlight that AI-­enhanced SEL significantly boosts student engagement and emotional well-­being. By providing tailored learn- ing experiences based on students' emotional and cognitive needs, AI systems facilitate better emotional regulation, increased focus and improved academic performance. The results suggest that AI-­enhanced SEL frameworks offer personalised support that not only enhances learning outcomes but also creates a more emotionally supportive environment, contributing to students' overall academic success and well-­being.
